text:
anya: Quick q — how should we expose SLO-driven fallback policies per customer? I want to propose a 'soft fallback' mode that routes to a smaller/quantized model variant when latency threatens the SLO but availability still holds. Does that fit with console + runtime constraints?
caleb: I like tying it to customer tier SLOs instead of raw latency thresholds. Example: gold P95 latency target = 150ms, silver = 300ms. If region can't meet the tier SLO, trigger fallback. Also need a circuit-breaker to avoid oscillation.
sophia: Agree on tier-based SLOs. For telemetry we need per-customer, per-region rolling windows for success_rate and latency. What window do we want — 1m for rapid response or 5m for smoothing?
raj: 5m rolling for steady-state; 1m window as a panic detector. CB open if fail_rate > 5% over 1m OR p95_latency > configured_slo * 1.4. That gives headroom to avoid false positives.
anya: Those numbers look reasonable. UX requirements: console should show policy state (open/closed/degraded), the trigger reason, and a manual override (force fallback / disable). Also let rules be 'soft' (degrade model) vs 'hard' (reject or route to offline variant).
kevin: Internal API question — do we evaluate the policy inline in the request path or call a policy-service? Inline gives fastest reaction but adds code/latency in hot path. Policy-service simplifies logic but adds a network hop. Thoughts?
caleb: We already have route-decider middleware inside runtime. Could extend it to consult a local read-only cache of policies updated by a push from the control plane. So no extra RPC per request but still central control.
sophia: Telemetry/event model: emit a route_decision event for every decision with fields: customer_id, region, tier, model_variant, decision_reason, estimated_latency_ms, token_count, policy_id. Also sample full traces for 1/100 requests. That will let us correlate policy flips with customer impact.
anya: Example policy snippet for the console/API (WIP):
```json
{
  "policy_id": "fallback_v2",
  "target_tiers": ["gold","silver"],
  "region_scope": ["us-east-1","eu-west-1"],
  "mode": "soft",       // soft = lower-quality model, hard = reject/fallback-to-archive
  "slo_p95_ms": 150,
  "cb": { "window_sec": 60, "fail_rate_pct": 5, "latency_multiplier": 1.4 }
}
```
This could be created/edited in Console and pushed to edge caches.
raj: Rollouts: support rollout_pct so we can canary the fallback (e.g., pct=10). Also tag rollouts with rollout_id to track. Console should show active rollout pct.
kevin: Quota interaction: note that changing model_variant may alter tokenization/cost. We need to estimate cost delta and show it during policy creation and in telemetry (cost_estimate_delta).
caleb: Observability: dashboard per-policy with p95 latency, fail_rate, cb_state timeline, effected_customers list, and a rollback button that opens a change request. Also link to sampled traces.
sophia: I'll mock the Console screens and telemetry schema. Needs an event-bus topic (policy-decisions) and a mapping document for downstream billing/alerts. Tagging: policy_id, rollout_id, decision_reason.
anya: Cool — I'll open a runtime PR to add the local policy cache + emit route_decision events. Assign to myself and raj for CB logic.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: policy-cache branch -> staging at 2026-03-19 04:00 UTC :rocket:
kevin: One more: add an audit log entry whenever a human toggles a policy override (who, when, reason). That should be part of compliance for private deployments.
anya: ack — will include audit events. Next step: design doc + small API spec (read-only policy cache push + admin CRUD).
